It’s all part of the responsibility I have to ensure she’s kept in the best possible condition. And it’s convenient for her too. It keeps her modest at all times, removing the need for her to unmask in public or deal with the inconvenience of a privacy cabin.”
Mara’s focus remained on the rhythmic pulsing of the gag. Each time it released a portion of the nutrient liquid, she braced herself, swallowing quickly to avoid the discomfort of the liquid pooling in her mouth and blocking her breathing. Her throat worked mechanically, the taste of the nutrient bland and slightly salty—nothing like the rich flavors of the dinner being served to the others.
Despite the humiliation, Mara knew she had to maintain her composure. Her role was to sit quietly, hands folded, posture perfect, and to endure the feeding process with the same grace and submission expected of her in every other aspect of her life. The discomfort, the control, the loss of even this basic autonomy—it all served as a constant reminder of her place.
Philippe turned slightly toward Mara, resting his hand affectionately on the back of her chair. “Mara is adapting well to this new system,” he continued, addressing the diplomat but clearly speaking as much for Mara’s benefit. “It’s a matter of training, really. Teaching her body to accept and process the nourishment in this way. She’s made excellent progress.”
The diplomat smiled approvingly. “You’re doing an admirable job, Philippe. It’s clear she’s in very good hands.”
Mara’s eyes remained fixed forward, her breathing steady and controlled. She swallowed again, the nutrient liquid sliding down her throat, and she forced herself to focus on the rhythm, on the routine of it.
Much later that evening, after the dinner was over and the guests had said their goodbyes, Mara finally lay in bed, her body encased in the rigid shell of the iGuardian. It was her first night experiencing the full extent of the device’s restrictions, and every sensation was new and unsettling. Philippe had undressed her down to mask, gloves, stockings, and boots, with the corset, neck corset, and shoulder braces relaxed for the night.
He attached restraints to her legs, locking them apart by about a meter, and connected a restraint and charging cable to the attachment point between her shoulder blades. “There,” he said quietly. “You should be able to rest comfortably now, but you’ll always be aware of your boundaries.” Mara could only lie still as Philippe finished his adjustments.
As Philippe stepped back, satisfied with his work, he gave her a brief nod. “Good night, Mara. Rest well.”
“Good night, Sir,” Mara signed, her hands moving slowly.
Left alone in the darkness, Mara explored the iGuardian with her gloved hands, trying to familiarize herself with the device’s contours. Her fingers traced the hard lines of the breast covers, the smooth, unyielding surface of the crotch cover. But as soon as her touch lingered too close to these areas, a searing pain shot through her from the electrodes embedded in the device. It was a sharp, intense correction, reminding her not to breach her chastity device’s strict limits.
Gasping silently, Mara quickly withdrew her hands, the lesson clear. Any attempt to touch herself, even unintentionally, would be met with severe consequences. Chastity was not just expected; it was enforced with an iron grip. She learned to keep her hands far from the restricted areas, every movement calculated to avoid another correction.
The hours of the night stretched on, each moment a lesson in stillness and restraint. The tension in her body never fully eased, the ever-present pressure of the iGuardian and the restraints keeping her on edge, even in sleep.
When morning came, the device automatically released Mara from her night’s confinement. The restraint at her back unclipped with a soft click, and the ankle restraints retracted, allowing her to move again, though the iGuardian remained securely in place.
Mara carefully sat up, a task made challenging by the rigid iGuardian that prevented her from bending or twisting her torso. She had to shift her legs to the side and use her arms to push herself up. As she moved to the edge of the bed, she used both hands to ease the pressure from the crotch cover. Though her corset had been slightly loosened for sleep, it still required her full attention as she maneuvered out of bed.
As soon as she stood, the corset, braces, and neck support automatically tightened to their daytime settings. The sudden adjustment nearly threw her off balance. Dressing herself was even harder now in the iGuardian than it had been before, but Mara tried to handle it alone, clinging to the small bit of independence it allowed her.
She quickly dressed, putting on her Yoyah Sheengzoh and a Victorian-style dressing gown over her gloves, stockings, and boots. With this daily routine finished, she headed to the kitchen to prepare Philippe’s morning tea. Every move was cautious, knowing that any mistake could trigger a painful correction from the iGuardian. Balancing the tray, she walked carefully down the hallway, keeping her posture as perfect as the device demanded, before reaching Philippe’s study.
Entering the study, she found Philippe already seated at his desk, reading through a stack of documents. She paused, steadying herself before she moved forward. Both hands full with the tray of tea, she couldn’t sign, so she approached silently.
Philippe glanced up, a slight smile on his lips. “Good morning, Mara. You may serve the tea.”
Mara positioned herself beside the table, moving with care. She knew from the day before how crucial it was to maintain the correct posture at all times. The iGuardian was unforgiving in its expectations.
She bent at the knees, keeping herself upright, and managed to set the cup down without triggering a correction. The relief was brief, but she felt a small measure of satisfaction in completing the task without incident.
Philippe observed her closely, his gaze sharp as he took in every detail. “You’re improving,” he noted with approval. “Who would have thought that all you needed was structure and a bit of discipline?”
“Thank you, Sir, and a good morning to you, too,” Mara signed, her hands finally free. Inside, she felt the familiar mix of frustration and resignation. Every movement took so much effort, so much attention, that even the simplest tasks left her exhausted. Yet, she knew she had no choice but to continue, to adapt to these new restrictions until they became second nature.
As she stood back, waiting for Philippe’s next instruction, she reminded herself of the lessons learned so far. The iGuardian was not just a device—it was her life now, dictating every aspect of her existence. To survive, she had to find peace in the stillness and in the careful, deliberate movements it demanded. And so, Mara began to learn, each day a lesson in the restraint, submission, and formality that her role required.

title: Chapter 41: The Charity Gala commences
content:
The Charity Gala commences# Philippe carefully supported Mara as she walked through the ballroom, her dress allowing only minimal steps. He led her to a tether bar where two other women waited for their guardians. Philippe clicked Mara into the bar, then stepped back to look for staff and Tom Holland to follow up on that affair. Zendaya’s rebellion would make for an interesting evening.
The women beside her were unmistakably Saudi, their faces veiled behind layers of gauze, exposing only their eyes. The inner veils were dark and mysterious, covered by an outer veil made of gold coins that jingled softly. Their hair was hidden beneath embroidered niqabs, and each abaya was adorned with flower patterns. The older woman’s abaya had red hues with desert roses and Arabian jasmine, while the younger’s abaya had white and yellow flowers like Arabian primrose and desert marigold. Chains clinked beneath their attire when they shifted.
Mara, feeling the constraints of her dress, began the formal introduction. “Philippe Beaumont’s Mara,” she signed.
The older woman responded warmly, “Abdulaziz Al-Faraj’s Layla.”
The younger followed, “Hassan Al-Saud’s Amina.”
With formalities done, they began to converse more informally.
“Mara, your outfit is breathtaking,” Layla said. “It must be demanding to wear.”
Mara signed amusement. “Thank you, Layla. It is literally breathtaking. Ballet and yoga help me manage.”
Amina’s eyes sparkled. “That’s impressive, Mara. I can’t imagine wearing something so restrictive with such grace.”
Mara’s barked arms signed thanks for the compliment, and she continued. “Your outfits are stunning too. I noticed the sound of chains. Are they symbolic?”
Layla nodded, the coins on her veil chiming softly. “They are very real and solid, but they also have a symbolic meaning. The chains show our guardians are wealthy and can afford women who never have to work. It’s a matter of pride and status since the Change.”
Amina added, “They are permanent, welded on as is customary. We wear them with pride, showcasing our guardians’ care and our commitment to our roles.”
Mara listened, understanding the cultural significance and shared experiences of strict societal expectations. “That is fascinating. It must require a lot of dedication.”
Layla’s eyes crinkled in a smile. “It does. But we are honored to wear them and have help. Being chained means having a maid to take care of many daily needs.”
Their discussion turned to fitness. Mara, feeling the constraints of her stiff tree-like dress, started the discussion. “I’ve found that wearing a long-term chastity belt presents certain challenges, especially in maintaining flexibility and strength. I rely on yoga and ballet.”
Layla brightened. “Yoga and ballet sound wonderful, Mara. I’ve heard they are excellent for flexibility. How do you manage the exercises with the belt on?”
Mara smiled slightly. “I’ve adapted many poses to accommodate the belt. It’s about finding the right balance and being gentle with your body.”
Amina nodded. “That’s impressive, Mara. For us, being chained presents challenges. We rely on tailored exercises that focus on the areas we can move freely.”
Layla elaborated, “We do a lot of seated and standing exercises. Resistance bands are great for working our arms and legs within our limited range of motion. We also practice a modified form of Tai Chi, which helps with balance and flexibility without needing wide movements.”
Mara’s eyes widened with interest. “Tai Chi sounds perfect. I might try some of those movements. Do you find it difficult to stay motivated?”
Amina chuckled softly. “Motivation can be a challenge, but our guardians support us and provide us with the… encouragement we need. We also have a maid who assists with our exercises, ensuring our routine is safe.”
Philippe returned with a tray of snacks and drinks. He offered water in a bag to Mara, making light-hearted jokes that elicited soft laughter from Amina and Layla.
“You probably need plenty of water, Mara. You know, photosynthesis and all,” he teased, connecting the bag.
Mara smiled, her eyes crinkling with amusement. “Thank you, Sir,” she signed, feeling the cool water refresh her throat.
Meanwhile, the charity auction was in full swing. Zendaya, despite her restrictive outfit and gag, moved with practiced elegance. Her elbow and knee joints were visibly locked, adding to her restraints.
She presented various items gifted by celebrities to the audience. The auctioneer, a charismatic man named Charles Dupont, described each item with enthusiasm, his voice resonating through the ballroom.
“Ladies and gentlemen, our next item is a one-of-a-kind necklace donated by Harry Styles!” Charles announced. “This stunning piece features rare emeralds set in platinum.”
Zendaya presented the necklace with stretched arms, the stage lights catching the brilliant green of the emeralds. The audience gasped in admiration, the wards encouraging their guardians to bid.
“We’ll start the bidding at ten thousand euros. Do I hear ten thousand?” Charles called out.
A hand shot up. “Ten thousand!” a man near the front shouted.
“Fifteen thousand!” another man quickly countered, his ward clapping excitedly beside him.
The bids climbed rapidly. “Twenty thousand! Twenty-five thousand!” Charles called out.
“Thirty thousand!” a voice from the back rang out. It was Lord Hargreaves, his presence commanding respect. Caroline, his ward, stood beside him, her veiled head held high in pride.
“Thirty thousand from Lord Hargreaves! Do I hear thirty-five?” Charles urged.
“Forty thousand!” came the next bid, from a distinguished man in a sharp suit. His ward, dressed in an elegant gown adorned with ivy, beamed with delight.
The room buzzed with excitement. Philippe and Mara watched with interest.
“Fifty thousand! Fifty-five thousand!” Charles kept the momentum going.
“Sixty thousand!” the man in the sharp suit bid again.
“Going once, going twice…” Charles paused. “Sold! To the gentleman in the sharp suit for sixty thousand euros! Congratulations!”
The room erupted in applause, the successful bidder receiving pats on the back from nearby guests. His ward looked up at him with admiration, clearly proud of his win.
“Next, we have an exclusive vacation package to a private island in the Maldives, donated by Leonardo DiCaprio!” Charles announced, moving seamlessly to the next item. Zendaya, moving around with rigid knees, presented the package with a flourish, the imagery of pristine beaches and luxury accommodations captivating the audience.
“Bidding starts at twenty thousand euros,” Charles began, the room coming alive with excitement.
As the bids soared, Philippe leaned in close to Mara. “The enthusiasm tonight is incredible. The funds raised will do so much good.”
Mara nodded, her eyes shining. “Yes, Sir. It’s wonderful to see such generosity. This will make a significant impact.”
The charity auction continued, each item fetching impressive sums. Mara and Philippe observed with satisfaction, knowing their efforts had paid off.

title: Chapter 42: Two years earlier: Breaking Point
content:
Two years earlier: Breaking Point# Mara knelt on her cushion on the polished marble floor of Philippe’s study, her back perfectly straight, her hips pushed upright, and her shoulders held back in the exact posture the iGuardian demanded. She had grown accustomed to the feel of the Yoyah Sheengzoh underskirt constricting her legs, but it was the act of sitting that had become a challenge she for now avoided. Kneeling, she had learned, it was far easier to maintain the required posture. It also avoided the painful pressure on the crotch belt that shifted her entire iGuardian upwards whenever she sat too far back on the chair, and it presented a more submissive stance that Philippe seemed to appreciate.
Philippe was in the middle of a conversation with a visiting diplomat, his voice steady and commanding as he discussed trade agreements. Mara remained silent, her hands folded neatly in her lap, her eyes downcast. She was the picture of calm composure, even though her muscles ached from the tension of holding her body in this precise position for so long.
As the diplomat made a sharp remark, questioning a decision Philippe had made, Mara’s instinct was to respond—to defend Philippe, to correct the visitor’s impolite tone. But she caught herself, knowing that such an outburst would only result in a painful correction from the iGuardian. Instead, she focused on her breathing, ensuring it remained steady, and when Philippe addressed her with a glance, she responded with a polite affirmative hand sign and nothing more.
When the meeting ended, Philippe dismissed the diplomat and turned his attention to Mara. “You may stand now,” he instructed and offered a hand.
Mara slowly rose to her feet, careful to keep her posture perfect as she did so. She moved with the grace of a dancer, each step a careful glide, her weight evenly distributed. She had learned, over the past few weeks, how to rise without disturbing the balance the iGuardian enforced.
Philippe studied her for a moment, then gestured to a pair of boots on a nearby stool. “Today, we’re going to try something different,” he said.
Mara’s eyes fell on the boots—ballet boots, with an impossibly high arch that forced the wearer onto their toes. She felt a flicker of apprehension but quickly quelled it. She had learned not to question Philippe’s decisions. Instead, she waited silently as he retrieved the boots and gestured for her to sit.
Mara carefully lowered herself onto the edge of a nearby chair. Philippe knelt and began changing her boots for the new ones. The moment she tried to stand, she felt her balance shift dramatically, her body forced into a position that was all too familiar.
“Up on your toes now,” Philippe said, guiding her into position. “You’ll find this helps with your posture.”
Mara stood, feeling the tight stretch in her calves as the boots forced her into an en pointe position. The sensation was both uncomfortable and strangely familiar, reminding her of her days as a ballet student. She adjusted her stance, focusing on keeping her balance, and found that the boots did indeed make it easier to maintain the posture Philippe expected of her. The arch forced her hips upright, her chest naturally pushed out as she aligned herself with the strict requirements of the iGuardian.
“Good,” Philippe said, stepping back to observe her. “You see? These boots will help you maintain the correct posture without as much effort.”
Over the next few days, Mara grew accustomed to the ballet boots. She found herself moving with even more grace, the lessons from her ballet training merging with the demands of the iGuardian to create a sense of fluidity in her movements. She knelt more often, preferring the ease it offered compared to sitting, and her posture became second nature.
Then, one day, as Mara stood before Philippe, her posture perfect and her hands folded neatly in her lap, he looked her over with a pleased expression.
“I must say, Mara, I’m impressed,” Philippe said, his voice calm and even. “Your behavior has improved significantly. You’re a different woman now—thanks to the iGuardian. Who would have thought it could be so simple?”
Philippe’s words echoed in Mara’s mind, striking her like a cold wave. Simple? Did he really think that everything she had gone through was simple? The months of constant pressure, the relentless control, the loss of every shred of autonomy—did he truly believe that her transformation had been easy?
The thought ignited a fire inside her, and before she could stop herself, Mara’s hands flew up, signing furiously at Philippe. Her movements were sharp, angry, her gestures obscene. She poured out her frustration, her rage, her despair—she wanted him to understand just how much she had suffered, how much she still suffered, trapped in the iGuardian with no escape.
But as her hands moved, Mara knew she had made a terrible mistake. The iGuardian detected her defiance almost instantly, and without warning, it switched into discipline mode. Pain shot through her body, searing and relentless, as the electrodes in her most sensitive areas activated. The shocks were harsh, punishing her for her outburst. But despite the pain, Mara’s resolve didn’t waver. She gritted her teeth, her body tensing but refusing to give in completely. She had endured worse—pain was something she could push through.
Philippe watched her closely, his expression shifting as he observed her response. When the shocks finally ceased, Mara stood trembling, not from fear but from the sheer physical toll. Her anger was still there, simmering beneath the surface, but now mixed with a deep sense of frustration. The pain, though intense, had not taught her as Philippe had hoped.
Philippe realized that something was wrong. The approach he had relied on—the use of pain to enforce discipline—was not having the desired effect on Mara. In fact, it was only hardening her resistance. He could see it in her eyes, in the way she held herself even after the correction. Pain, he suddenly understood, wasn’t the answer for someone like Mara.
In that moment, Philippe realized he needed a different approach. Pain wasn’t working with Mara, so he searched through the iGuardian’s control app for an alternative. His eyes landed on edging mode. He decided to try it—pleasure, not pain, might be what Mara responded to.
With a firm tap, Philippe activated the program. The iGuardian immediately began to stimulate Mara, focusing on her most sensitive areas with relentless precision. The sensation took her by surprise, overwhelming her. Her breath quickened, her body reacting instinctively, her legs trembling as the device kept her on the edge of satisfaction without ever letting her reach it. Her hands wandered, drawn to the stimulated areas, but she had already learned and internalized the restriction that she was not allowed to touch herself. Unsure where to put her hands and what to do with them, she gesticulated, desire melting her mind.
For the first time, Mara couldn’t push through what she was feeling. She was used to enduring pain, but this was different. The iGuardian adapted to her responses, keeping her in a constant state of unfulfilled need. The anticipation, the teasing, the possibility of release—it was impossible to ignore.
“Mara,” Philippe said quietly, watching her closely, “you’ll learn. You’re already on your way.”
Mara didn’t respond. She was completely overwhelmed by the iGuardian’s new strategy.
As the days passed, the iGuardian continued its relentless conditioning. Mara quickly learned that any sign of defiance or misstep would lead to the withdrawal of the stimulation she had come to crave. This withdrawal alone was enough to motivate her toward compliant behavior. The desire to be a “Good Girl” and maintain that constant, tantalizing stimulation became her driving force. If she still resisted, the iGuardian resorted to painful corrections, but the pain was less effective than her growing need to avoid the absence of pleasure.
Deep down, Mara knew the iGuardian would never grant her release. But the constant stimulation, the teasing, the hope that maybe, just maybe, Philippe would eventually allow her the satisfaction she longed for, drove her to new levels of obedience. She started seeking ways to please Philippe, to avoid the painful corrections, and to keep the stimulation going for as long as possible.
Her posture, once something she had to think about, became automatic. She spoke with extreme politeness and deference, never raising her voice or showing any sign of the frustration that still simmered beneath the surface.
Philippe noticed the change. “You’ve come a long way, Mara,” he remarked one day, watching her as she knelt before him, after a day of flawless demeanor. “I hoped you would finally make progress, but you’ve exceeded my expectations.”
Mara’s hands moved smoothly and gracefully as she responded, “Thank you, Sir. With your guidance, I’m trying to be the best I can be.”
She knew she was being conditioned, trained into obedience, but there was no escape. Day by day, the iGuardian stripped away her resistance, molding her into the obedient, submissive woman society demanded her to be.
Satisfied with her progress, Philippe decided to reward her. He leaned over, disabling the edging mode on the iGuardian. He set the device to deliver a full reward with release, and also ordered her to come. The sudden wave of pleasure that followed left Mara breathless, her body trembling from the intensity of it. For a brief moment she teetered on the edge, then she experienced the crashing wave of release she had been denied for days.
Philippe watched her with a pleased expression. “Good girl, Mara,” he said, his voice warm. “You’ve earned this.”
Mara, still catching her breath, signed her gratitude. “Thank you, Sir.”
The iGuardian remained in place, its control over her as unyielding as ever. Philippe had granted her a rare release, and also had finally turned the relentless edging off.
At least that is what it felt like for Mara. Unbeknownst to her, the mode continued to run in the background at a very low level, subtly shaping her behavior. The constant, barely noticeable stimulation persisted, reinforcing her obedience by quietly withdrawing whenever she approached undesirable behavior. The conditioning continued, now operating below her conscious awareness, guiding her toward the submission she needed to learn.

title: Chapter 43: Kidnapped!
content:
Kidnapped!# The Green Gala at the Ecoville Hotel was ending. Guests, still excited, made their way to their vehicles. Zendaya, in her metallic red fembot suit covered with flowers and leaves, approached her hexacopter with Tom Holland’s help. The suit was now almost completely locked, making her unable to move without assistance.
As Tom helped Zendaya into the hexacopter, the sudden noise of engines pierced the night air. Two black motorbikes stopped nearby. The riders, four figures in dark clothing and wearing advanced breather masks, leaped off their bikes.
“Get away from her!” Tom shouted, stepping forward. One assailant shoved him to the ground.
“Get back, everybody!” a masked figure barked, waving a compact, but dangerously looking weapon. The crowd scattered in fear. The hexacopter’s engines buzzed to life, the blades spinning faster and faster. Zendaya, struggling in her suit, was secured in a seat, her eyes wide with shock behind the fembot hood.
“Call the Grenadiers!” someone shouted. Philippe, watching from a distance, pulled out his cellphone and called for help. “We need immediate assistance at the Ecoville Hotel! There’s been a kidnapping!”
As the hexacopter lifted off, the two remaining attackers revved their engines and sped away on their motorbikes, weaving through the guests, and speeding down the grand driveway. Sirens echoed as the Grenadiers arrived with flashing light.
“Don’t let them escape!” an officer yelled. The chase began through Geneva’s narrow streets. the bikes navigated the network of sidestreets, making sharp turns. The Grenadiers followed closely, using advanced tracking systems.
Eliza, one of the bikers, looked back. “They’re gaining on us, Max! We need to split up!” she shouted.
Max nodded. “Take the left alley! I’ll draw them away!” He veered right, leading some Grenadiers away. Eliza sped down a narrow alley, her bike skidding.
The Grenadiers split up, some following Max, others tailing Eliza. Max turned a final corner, saw Grenadiers in front of him, while others caught up behind him. Realizing he was cornered, he skidded to a stop, his bike crashing against a wall. He stood weapon in hand as the Grenadiers surrounded him.
“Drop the weapon! You’re surrounded!” a Grenadier shouted.
Max hesitated, but realized he was outnumbered and outgunned. He dropped the weapon, raising his hands in surrender.
Eliza, trapped in a cul-de-sac, tried to turn back but was blocked. She revved her engine, considering a reckless escape, but the Grenadiers had her surrounded. “Stand down! There’s no way out,” an officer said as he stepped forward. Eliza recognized him—Captain Duval, a man she had once respected before the Change. She sighed, knowing the fight was over, dismounted and raised her hands.
Inside the hexacopter, Zendaya struggled, held down by a female captor. The male captor, piloting the craft, flew unsteadily. Zendaya’s muffled attempts to speak went unheard. The female captor tightened her grip. “Stay still, and it will be easier for you,” she whispered.
The hexacopter flew low over the dark waters of the lake, then following the River Rhône. The copter almost skimming treetops, weaving through narrow valleys. The absence of any pursuers confused them, but they didn’t have time to question their luck, when they eventually veered into a side-valley, up the Lonza River as they approached the Aletsch Glacier. Suddenly, the pilot executed a sharp dive, bringing the copter down towards a tiny, newly built hut next to a small landing pad. The lading was rough in the winds of the high alps,and the pilot exhaled in relief and ordered, “Get her out, quickly.”
The female captor dragged Zendaya across the landing pad into the hut, securing her to a chair. “We’ll be safe here for now,” she said, her voice muffled by her breather.
Outside, the male captor secured and folded the hexacopter, concealing it from prying eyes. But this high up they were alone, the sound of distant running water was the only he could hear.
Inside, Zendaya’s eyes searched for a way out. The gagged fembot mask restricted her vision, and she was throughly bound. Her female captor watched the door nervously.
“We have to move quickly,” the male captor said as he entered the hut, closing the door behind him. “The Freeborn Alliance will send someone to pick us up soon.”
The man moved towards Zendaya, removing her robot headpiece with special tooling. Zendaya gasped for breath, her voice finally freed. “Help me, please,” she cried, tears streaming down her face. “It hurts.”
The man frowned confused. “What hurts?”
“My belt,” she whimpered. “I am outside the geofence. It keeps zapping me.”
A stream of expletives flew from the man’s mouth. “Damn it! No wonder we weren’t followed,” he muttered. “She’s in an active chastity device. They all have tracking beacons!”
He looked at his female companion. “Quick! Help me get this off her! We need to silence the beacon!”
They fumbled with her suit as Zendaya’s sobs filled the hut while they worked, the pain from the belt’s zaps making her body twitch involuntarily.
Suddenly, flashbang grenades exploded, blinding and deafening them. The kidnappers were disoriented, stumbling back and covering their ears. The door burst open, and a team of Commandement des Forces Spéciales, equipped with goggles and tactical gear, stormed in, firing stun ammo at the two kidnappers. The air was filled with shouted commands and the thud of boots as doors were kicked in.
“Clear!” one of the Grenadiers shouted, securing the room.
Outside, the sound of helicopter blades grew louder. An alpine rescue emergency doctor abseiled down, followed by more heavily armed special forces. The kidnappers were bound, dragged out of the hut, and lifted into the helicopter.
The emergency doctor quickly assessed Zendaya, and cut through her suit and belt using specialized equipment, finally freeing her. Zendaya winced as the belt came off, still crying from the pain. “You’re going to be okay,” the doctor said softly, applying a mild sedative and wrapping her in a warm blanket. She was lifted out of the hut on a rescue stretcher and pulled up into the helicopter.
As the helicopter ascended and headed towards Geneva, Zendaya’s eyes fluttered closed, exhaustion and the sedative pulling her under. The ordeal was over, and she was safe again.

title: Chapter 44: After the Gala
content:
After the Gala# Mara’s day ended early in the morning, her body exhausted from the evening’s events and the restrictive clothing she wore. Every step was a struggle, and every smile carefully balanced against the demands of her dress. The evening started with a crisis when Zendaya arrived bare-faced, breaking important social rules. Mara managed the situation, but her relief was short-lived when Zendaya was kidnapped by unknown terrorists. Now, as she prepared for bed, the uncertainty about Zendaya’s fate left Mara deeply worried.
Philippe guided her to their suite, steadying her as she took unsteady steps. The stiff ballet boots provided extra support, for which she felt grateful. The recent events weighed heavily on their minds, and the anxiety was still fresh.
Entering the suite, they found Liliane asleep in a chair, still in her uniform. Philippe gently woke her, and together they began to remove Mara’s restrictive outfit. The headdress came off first, providing a welcome relief from its weight.
Philippe’s phone buzzed with a message. His face softened with relief as he read it. “Mara,” he said softly, “Zendaya has been rescued. All four kidnappers have been caught.”
Mara’s tense muscles relaxed at his words. “Thank God,” she signed. “Do we know who they were or why they did this?”
Philippe shook his head. “Not yet. They were very well-equipped but badly trained. It’s unclear who they are or what they wanted.”
Mara hand-danced her disappointment and unease. “It’s unsettling to think such a well-funded group is out there.”
“I know,” Philippe said, squeezing her hand. “But for now, Zendaya is safe, and the immediate threat is over. We’ll find out more in time.”
She tried to take comfort in his words. “I hope so. This night was more than I expected.”
Philippe offered a reassuring smile. “We’ll handle it, Mara. Together.”
They continued the careful process of undressing her, removing the stiff layers that encased her. With each piece removed, Mara felt both relief and a growing sense of vulnerability. Philippe held her steady while Liliane removed each part of her dress.
Once Mara could move freely again, Philippe and Liliane finished undressing her, leaving her in only her iGuardian. Philippe then sent Liliane off with the pieces of Mara’s dress, wishing her a good night.
The shift from the restrictive dress to the iGuardian left Mara feeling exposed. Philippe slipped a pair of high heels onto her feet—flat shoes were out of the question after years of wearing ballet heels. The height felt comfortable compared to the constant strain of the ballet boots.
He then led her to the bathroom for a quick wash. The iGuardian took care of most of the process, but Philippe hand-washed her exposed skin with gentle care. His touch was soothing, washing away the tension of the evening. The warmth of the water and his hands eased her aching body. He helped her remove her mask so she could brush her teeth, and then guided her to the bed.
As was their routine, he had her kneel by the bed so he could do her hair. He let down her bun, untangled the braids, but only did the necessary care, sensing how tired she was. His fingers moved through her hair with skill, lulling Mara into a near-sleep state. She was almost asleep when he relaxed the collar, braces, and corset of the iGuardian, lifted her into bed, and cuffed her arms in front of her, ensuring she was secure but comfortable.
Mara barely noticed when Philippe spooned against her, his body warm and comforting against the hard surface of the iGuardian. His warmth and presence kept the nightmares of the kidnapping away. Instead, she dreamed of the evening’s successes, feeling safe knowing Philippe was there to protect her.
Mara woke the next morning, still in darkness. The room was quiet except for Philippe’s gentle breathing behind her. She felt the firm embrace of the iGuardian, her feet elevated in heels, and the restriction of her cuffs. But despite this, she felt vulnerable. Her legs were bare, her arms ungloved, her mouth unfilled, and her face uncovered. This sense of exposure unsettled her.
As she stirred, Philippe woke up, sensing her discomfort. He shifted closer, offering comfort. She took a deep breath and spoke softly.
“Sir, may I please have my mask?” Her voice, almost unused over the last three years, was hoarse. Mara hated speaking, preferring the elegance and precision of hand-dancing, but with her hands cuffed, she had no other way to communicate. “I feel insecure without it.”
Philippe understood right away. “Of course, Mara,” he replied gently, reaching for the nightstand. He picked up her Jurenmuse and turned back to her, placing the gag in her mouth and locking the mask to her collar. The snug fit and pressure around her face made her feel safer.
“Thank you, Sir,” Mara tried to say, but only a satisfied moan escaped.
Philippe smiled, caressing her shoulder. “You’re welcome, Mara. Feel better now?”
Mara cuddled back against Philippe as much as she could within the stiff iGuardian, feeling relieved. His warmth and the mask’s security helped her relax again.
She drifted back to sleep, her mind at ease. The protective iGuardian and Philippe’s presence allowed her to surrender to the comforting darkness, feeling loved and cared for.
The next morning, Philippe guided her through the morning cleaning and dressing routine with care. He helped her into stockings and gloves, ensuring every seam was aligned. After securing her high-collared blouse and hobble skirt, he put her into a Victorian bustle dress again.
“Ready, Mara?” Philippe asked softly, checking her dress one last time.
“Yes, Sir,” Mara signed.
Philippe activated the her iGuardian’s guidance, and it sent her down to the breakfast room. She stood waiting at the entrance, in line with other women waiting for their guardians. When Philippe arrived, he led her over to his table and locked her into her chair.
A maid in the hotel’s uniform, her name tag read “Iris,” responded to Philippe’s signal. She attached a feed bag to the port on Mara’s mask and began serving Philippe his breakfast. Mara watched, feeling the slow expansion of the feed gag in her mouth, the nutrient liquid spurting down her throat. Her swallowing was automatic, years of training establishing themselves.
A few minutes later, Sonia and Henry entered. Henry, in a stylish suit, waved to Philippe, who gestured for them to join.
“Good morning, Philippe,” Henry greeted. “Good morning, Mara.”
“Good morning, Henry. Sonia,” Philippe replied.
Henry locked Sonia into the chair opposite Mara so that they could see each other. Sonia’s dress was equally elaborate but close-fitting: A blouse, buttoned in the back, and a floor-length mermaid skirt. For breakfast, she wore a niquab that would allow her to eat instead of a mask. As soon as Sonia was secured, her eyes met Mara’s, and they began signing to each other.
“Did you hear about Zendaya?” Sonia signed, serious.
Mara nodded, signing quickly. “Yes, Philippe told me this morning. She’s been rescued, and all four kidnappers have been caught.”
Henry leaned forward, looking at Philippe. “What do we know about the kidnappers?”
Philippe shook his head. “Not much yet. They were well-equipped but poorly trained. We don’t know who they are or their motives. It’s unsettling, to say the least.”
Sonia signed quickly, concern in her eyes. “Poor Zendaya. Do we know how she’s doing?”
“She’s safe and apparently unharmed,” Philippe reassured her. “She’s being taken care of and will be back soon.”
Mara and Sonia shared a deep sense of relief. “Thank goodness she’s safe. Last night was terrifying,” Mara signed.
Henry nodded. “We’ll need to stay vigilant. If there’s one group willing to go this far, there might be others.”
Philippe agreed. “Absolutely. We need to ensure everyone’s safety and be prepared for future threats.”
Sonia, sensing the need to lighten the mood, began hand-dancing with a hint of a smile. “Did you see Zendaya’s outfit last night? Despite everything, her transformation was fascinating. From a scandalously bare-faced human woman to an ever more robot-like being, all while incorporating elements of nature. It was quite a spectacle.”
Mara nodded, signing back. “Yes, it was intriguing. Her outfit became increasingly strict and mechanical. It’s amazing how fashion can reflect such contrasts. It also reminded me how important it is to maintain flexibility and muscle strength when wearing something as restrictive as a robot suit or my iGuardian."
Sonia’s eyes lit up. “Exactly! The strictness of our dress demands different fitness. It reminded me of Julien Moreau’s Anna. Before the Change, she was a runner. Now, she’s kept in shape with pony training. It’s rigorous but effective.”
Mara’s interest was piqued. “Pony training? I’ve heard of it but never seen it in practice. How does it work for her?”
Sonia signed enthusiastically, “It’s fascinating. Anna wears a special suit that restricts her and has a guide bit like a pony. She’s put in front of a sulky, and Julien guides her through an endurance course. It’s a combination of physical training and discipline.”
Mara nodded thoughtfully. “That sounds challenging and intriguing. I’d love to learn more about it. Maybe we could arrange a visit?”
Sonia’s hands moved eagerly. “I’m sure Anna would be happy to show you. She’s adapted well and enjoys the training now.”
Their conversation flowed seamlessly, their hands expressing what their voices couldn’t. Henry and Philippe watched with approval, pleased to see their wards engaged.
Philippe turned to Henry. “It’s good to see them connecting. They have a lot to share. Pony training sounds interesting. Mara could use more strength exercises, she’s so focused on mobility right now.”
Henry nodded warmly. “It’s quite demanding. It started as a discipline program for problematic women, focusing on obedience and submission, and also on keeping them exhausted. But a lot of well-adjusted women are doing it now, for fitness.”
Philippe and Henry agreed to explore the sport with their wards soon.

title: Chapter 45: A Day at the Races
content:
A Day at the Races# The opportunity came the following weekend when Philippe and Henry took their wards to the pony track. As they arrived, the place buzzed with excitement and order. The clinking of metal and leather being adjusted added to the strict atmosphere.
Anna was already on the track, dressed in her full pony outfit. Her catsuit was a striking shade of deep green, highlighting her toned body. The suit was seamless, with built-in gloves and feet, and her hair was pulled through a hole in her open-faced hood, cascading down her back. The suit left her derrière exposed, with only her chastity belt offering any modesty—a tempting target for the crop.
Over the catsuit, she wore a thick leather corset, dyed dark brown, cinching her waist tightly. It had attachment points at her hips for the sulky.
Her head was encased in an elaborate bridle, with cheekpieces, a noseband, and a throatlatch holding a bit in her mouth. The bit acted as a gag, preventing any speech. Originating from a discipline and obedience training program, it was made from rubber, but contained steel needles on the inside. It guided her, but if she resisted, the needles pressed into her mouth.
A wide, thick leather collar around her neck prevented any head movement, forcing Anna to follow the reins with her whole body. Blinkers attached to the cheekpieces restricted her vision, making her rely entirely on Julien’s guidance. An impressive plume matching her catsuit crowned her headstall.
Anna’s hands were locked to the sides of her corset with rigid leather arm sheaths, rendering them useless. Her feet were encased in knee-high pony boots, forcing her into an elevated foot position. The boots had heavy irons underneath.
Julien, her guardian and driver, adjusted the final straps and reins with care. He tested their tension with a gentle tug, ensuring they were responsive without immediately causing pain.
“Ready, Anna?” Julien asked, knowing she couldn’t respond verbally.
Anna’s gaze, narrowed by the blinkers, remained fixed ahead as she stood perfectly still, waiting for his command. Julien attached the sulky to her corset, securing it firmly and testing the connection. Satisfied, he took his place in the sulky, reins in hand.
“Walk on,” Julien commanded, touching Anna’s rear with the crop and letting the rein drop a bit.
Anna responded instantly, her body moving forward at the signal. She pulled the sulky towards the oval racetrack, her steps slow and cautious due to the weight of the cart and her restrictive outfit. Julien used the crop again, gently tapping her exposed rear, urging her to pick up the pace.
“Good girl, Anna. Keep going!” Julien encouraged.
Anna increased her pace, her legs working harder despite the strain of the pony boots and the weight of the irons. The blinkers limited her view, but she moved confidently, trusting Julien’s guidance. As they reached the track, Julien used the crop more frequently, tapping her rear to signal a faster pace.
“Go, go, go! Trot!” he ordered, his voice calm but firm.
Anna shifted to a trot. The irons under her boots clinked with each step, and her muscles strained under the effort. Julien maintained a gentle but firm grip on the reins, guiding her with precision. Any hint of disobedience was met with a sharper pull on the reins, a painful reminder to stay focused and compliant. Occasionally, he used the crop more sternly, delivering stinging corrections to her exposed rear.
Philippe and Henry watched with keen interest, noting Julien’s balanced approach of care and discipline with Anna. Philippe turned to Henry, clearly approving. “She’s well-trained. Julien has done an excellent job with her,” Philippe remarked.
Henry nodded, his eyes on Anna. “Indeed. She’s adapted well to the training. The discipline and control are impressive.”
Mara and Sonia, standing beside their guardians, observed silently. Mara was especially intrigued by the intensity of the training and the level of control Julien maintained. Sonia signed to Mara, her eyes wide with fascination.
“I’d like to try that someday. It looks intense but rewarding.”
Mara nodded, clearly interested. “Maybe we can arrange a session. It would be a good challenge.”
As Julien guided Anna around the track, her pace steadily increased. The physical and mental demands of the training were clear in her every movement. Despite the harshness of the exercise, there was a sense of purpose in her stride.
“Let’s pick up the pace. Go, go, go,” Julien commanded, giving Anna free rein.
Anna responded, her steps becoming more rhythmic and powerful. Julien’s guidance remained steady, his commands clear. The sulky moved smoothly behind her, showing off her strength and training.
After completing a fast-paced lap, Julien pulled the reins in a bit, slowing Anna to a controlled trot. The session continued, with Julien alternating between encouraging touches and sharper corrections, keeping a balance between discipline and support. After half an hour, it was clear Anna had reached her limits.
Philippe and Henry exchanged glances, impressed by the display of control and endurance. They knew this kind of training required not just physical strength but also mental toughness—qualities they valued highly in their wards.
As the session ended, Julien slowed Anna to a walk, allowing her to cool down. He dismounted and began unbuckling the straps, removing the reins. Anna stood still, her body trembling with exhaustion but her posture disciplined.
“Good work, Anna,” Julien said gently. “You did well today. Good girl!” Anna’s eyes, visible through the blinkers, showed her relief. She closed them as the praise triggered her conditioned response. The training had been tough, but she had endured and performed admirably.
Philippe turned to Mara, his voice filled with anticipation. “Are you interested in trying this, Mara? I have the necessary attachments for your iGuardian. It will be challenging, but I believe you can do it.”
Mara nodded, her eyes reflecting her determination. “Yes, Sir. I’m ready,” her hands danced.
Sonia looked startled, her hands signaling confusion. “Why would you need… Oh, you’re in a ‘Pro Secure’? I didn’t… That’s a lot more discipline than I expected.”
Philippe turned to her. “Yes, she is. But I have the pony training attachments available for it. We’ll see.”
Henry then turned to Sonia. “And you, would you like to try if we can find a fitting bridle in the stable?”
Sonia’s hands danced, expressing her interest. “I’d love to, Sir, but I’d rather not use someone else’s suit.”
Henry interrupted, “I know. As it happens…” He reached into the leather bag he carried and pulled out a pony training catsuit he had brought for her. Sonia’s eyes widened as she realized she had been set up.
While Julien helped Anna clean up and get dressed again, Henry guided Sonia to the changing area. There, he dressed her in a setup similar to what Anna had worn earlier. Sonia’s mind raced as she realized just how intense this was going to be.
Mara’s setup was simpler. The iGuardian already provided all the restraint and control necessary. Philippe added a bright pink latex catsuit over the device, ensuring it clung tightly to her form, highlighting her curves.
He then attached sulky connectors to the slots at her hips, clicking them securely into place. Next, Philippe laced her feet into knee-high pony boots, their elevated heels bringing her feet into a position she was used to.
Mara remained still, her hands folded neatly behind her back, as Philippe removed her regular mask and replaced it with a horse mask, complete with a pink plume. The mask was made of thick leather, with a built-in gag that filled her mouth. It clicked into the collar of her neck corset, fixing it in place. Finally, Philippe cuffed her hands behind her back. The restraints were simple but effective, leaving Mara with no way to resist or adjust herself.
Philippe guided her outside slowly, towards the sulkies. Sonia was already there, harnessed and waiting. Mara’s heart pounded in her chest, but she was ready for what was to come.
Philippe carefully attached the sulky to the fasteners on Mara’s iGuardian, making sure everything was secure. He then settled into the seat, holding a small controller connected via Bluetooth to her “virtual reins.” These “reins” sent impulses directly to Mara’s iGuardian, controlling the electrodes buried deep in her body and over her breasts. The impulses would guide her, signaling which direction to turn, when to speed up, and when to slow down.
“Ready, Mara?” Philippe asked, his voice calm but with an edge of anticipation.
Mara pawed her hooves, though her nerves were taut. She had no idea how intense this control would be, but she was determined to master it.
Philippe took a deep breath and signaled her to move forward. A sharp jolt surged through Mara’s body, the gag choking her gasp. The signal in her anus was far stronger than she had expected, almost painful. She instinctively twisted in the wrong direction, trying to ease the discomfort, but it only made the impulse worse.
Philippe was quickly easing off the control. He hadn’t anticipated just how sensitive the system was.
Mara bit down on her gag, stoically waiting for commands. Philippe made another attempt, this time with a gentler touch. The impulse came again, this time more bearable, though still uncomfortable. It guided her forward and to the right, but she hesitated, unsure of how much to turn. Philippe adjusted the reins, and the signal became sharper, almost punishing. Mara winced, feeling the pain deep inside and on her right breast, as the breast cover activated too.
Philippe, sensing Mara’s distress, nodded, focusing on making his movements smaller. He moved the controller more carefully, and this time, the impulse was softer. Mara felt it guiding her, not forcing her. She turned to the right, moving the sulky along with her, feeling more in tune with the signal. But then Philippe tried to make her stop, and the sudden sharp impulse to her clit made her stumble, the pain almost bringing her to her knees.
Philippe pulled back completely. He took a moment to recalibrate the controls in his mind, trying to find the balance.
They tried again. Philippe sent a softer signal, and Mara moved as directed, turning smoothly this time. When he wanted her to stop, he carefully applied just a bit more pressure on the controller, and the signals from the iGuardian pulsed in a way that was firm but not painful. Mara slowed, coming to a controlled stop.
A look of relief crossed Philippe’s face as he saw they were finally in sync. Mara’s body relaxed slightly, the pain subsiding as she adjusted to the guidance. They both had a better understanding now—Philippe of the delicacy required, and Mara of how to read the signals.
“Got it,” Philippe murmured, more to himself than to her. He sent another command, and this time, Mara responded perfectly, moving the sulky forward with a steady pace. They were finally working together.
With the controls mastered, Philippe guided Mara to the track where Sonia, now in her own sulky with Henry as her driver, was waiting. Both women stood side by side, harnessed and ready, their eyes focused ahead. Mara was smaller and lighter than Sonia, but she felt the challenge in the air. Her competitive spirit flared, and she was determined to win this race.
Julien stood at the starting line, holding up a flag. He looked over at the two sulkies, his eyes scanning both women and their drivers. The tension in the air was thick as everyone prepared for the race.
Mara bit down again on her gag, determined to win and to prove herself, mastering this new challenge despite the pain and the control. She glanced at Sonia, who seemed just as determined, and then back at the track ahead.
Julien raised the flag, ready to start the race.
The race began with a burst of energy. Henry drove Sonia with sharp taps of the crop on her exposed rear, urging her forward with every strike. Philippe, on the other hand, guided Mara using the impulses from her iGuardian, sending pulses deep into her body to push her ahead. Both women started side by side, but it didn’t take long for the differences in their physical abilities to show.
Sonia, in her sleek black catsuit, surged ahead, her powerful legs propelling her forward with ease. Mara, in her bright pink suit, struggled to keep up. She pushed herself hard, trying to match Sonia’s pace, but the race quickly became a battle of raw power, something Mara lacked compared to Sonia’s larger frame.
Philippe sensed Mara’s determination, saw how badly she wanted to win, and he pushed her harder with the signals, trying to draw out every ounce of energy she had. Mara responded, digging deep, her body straining with the effort. Her strength was in her flexibility and endurance, skills honed through years of ballet and yoga, but this race demanded something else—pure, brute strength. Despite her best efforts, Sonia continued to pull ahead, her powerful strides eating up the distance between them.
Mara felt the gap widen, felt the looming sense of failure creeping in. Her competitive spirit clashed with the reality of her limitations, and no matter how hard she tried, she couldn’t close the gap. Her legs burned, her lungs screamed for air, but it wasn’t enough. She watched helplessly as Sonia crossed the finish line well ahead of her.
By the time Mara stumbled across the line, she was exhausted and devastated. The victory had been so far out of reach, and now the weight of her failure settled on her heavily.
Philippe led her back to the changing rooms in silence. He could see the tears welling up in her eyes, the pain of her defeat written all over her face. Once inside, he gently began cleaning her, wiping away the sweat and grime, then helped her change back into her normal outfit and day-mask. The whole time, Mara fought back her tears, but when she was finally dressed, she couldn’t hold them back any longer. She broke down, crying quietly, the sting of failure cutting deep.
“I’m sorry, Sir,” Mara signed with trembling hands, tears streaming down behind eher mask. “I failed you, Sir.”
Philippe, kneeling and sitting her down on his knee in the stable, gently supporting her with one arm, watched her hands move with a sense of sorrow. He placed a hand gently around her narrow waist, his voice soft and reassuring. “Mara, you didn’t fail me. Please don’t think that.”
Mara hesitated, her fingers moving slowly, as if she was unsure whether to continue. “It feels like I did, Sir. I couldn’t keep up. I wasn’t strong enough. I couldn’t even come close to what you expected.”
Philippe shook his head, his tone firm but kind. “What I expected was for you to give your best, and you did that. Winning wasn’t the goal. You showed determination and spirit, and that’s what matters to me.”
Mara’s hands stilled for a moment, the weight of his words sinking in. But then, with a soft, almost hesitant gesture, she signed, “I wanted to make you proud, Sir. I didn’t want to disappoint you.”
Philippe’s expression softened even more, and he took one of her gloved hands in his. “Mara, you didn’t disappoint me. Your dedication and willingness to push yourself are what make me proud. You have nothing to be ashamed of. Enough for now.”
Mara nodded, her fingers moving slowly in a final sign. “Thank you, Sir, for your understanding.”
Later, the three women sat together on the veranda of Philippe’s villa in Cologny, each secured to her chair. Mara, masked and silent, was fed nutrients from a feed bag. Sonia and Anna, dressed in niqabs, carefully lifted their veils to enjoy their coffee and small slices of tarte tatin, the rich aroma of caramelized apples mingling with the fresh air.
Sonia’s fingers moved fluidly as she signed to Anna, “How was your training today? You looked amazing out there. How do you keep that speed for so long?”
Anna paused, then signed back, her movements slow and deliberate. “This was mild. Julien usually pushes me much harder. Lately, he’s been focused on obedience and endurance. I find comfort in the discipline and routine.”
Mara, watching the exchange, couldn’t help but snort behind her mask at the mention of comfort. She shifted slightly, the iGuardian pressing against her in all the familiar places. But Anna’s hands moved again, explaining further, her expression thoughtful.
“Yes, comfort,” she replied. “It might seem strange, but the discipline and routine give me a sense of purpose. When I’m pulling the sulky, it’s like everything else fades away. The noise in my head, the doubts—they all disappear. It’s just me, my body, and Julien’s guidance. I know my place, and I know what’s expected of me.” Peace within the boundaries set for me. It’s hard to explain, but I feel more myself in those moments than I do anywhere else."
Mara paused. She had not expected such a deep and serious answer. Thinking about her last two years in the iGuardian, she realized she understood more than she wanted to admit. The device had forced her into a similar kind of routine, where every movement was controlled, every action measured. There was no space for doubt or indecision; the device didn’t allow it. In a way, she had also found a strange peace within those boundaries, a place where the struggle to meet Philippe’s expectations became her sole focus. But unlike Anna, Mara wasn’t sure if she could ever call that peace comforting.
Sonia, always curious, tilted her head slightly as she signed to Mara. “I’ve never met anyone in an iGuardian Pro Secure before. What is it like?”
Mara paused, considering how to respond. The iGuardian was a part of her now, something she lived with every moment of every day. She wasn’t sure how to explain it, but she would try.
Her hands began to move slowly, with deliberate care. “It’s… constant. Every part of me is monitored, controlled. The device adjusts my posture, my movements, even my thoughts at times. It’s there to guide me, correct me, make sure I stay focused and disciplined.”
Sonia’s eyes widened slightly as she signed back. “Is it painful?”
Mara signed a “No”, her hands moving smoothly through the air. “Not if I do as I’m supposed to. But if I stray, if I forget my place, it can be… harsh. The impulses are strong, and they’re meant to teach me, to keep me in line.”
Anna, watching the exchange, nodded slightly, her eyes showing understanding. She signed, “It sounds difficult, but also… calming. Knowing what’s expected, having that guidance all the time.”
Mara hesitated, then nodded, her fingers echoing her agreement. “It is. There’s a certain peace in it. I don’t have to think about what’s right or wrong. The iGuardian decides that for me. It’s… freeing, in a way.”
Sonia’s hands paused before she signed again, her movements slow, thoughtful. “I never thought of it like that. I always imagined it would feel… restrictive.”
Mara’s hands moved quickly in response. “It is restrictive. But it’s also comforting. There’s no room for doubt, no room for error. Everything is decided for me, and that’s… easier.”
Sonia’s curiosity finally got the better of her. She glanced at Mara, her hands moving with a mix of concern and curiosity. “Mara, if I may ask, why are you in an iGuardian Pro Secure? I thought it was only used for women who disturb the harmony of society.”
Mara’s eyes flickered with a mix of emotions, but she quickly masked them. Her fingers moved with careful precision. “I made choices that led me here, Sonia. Philippe was right to use it. He has every right to expect the highest standards from his ward, and the iGuardian helps reinforce those standards.”
Sonia wasn’t entirely satisfied with the answer. She pressed on, her hands dancing with a hint of persistence. “But what about the rewards? Surely there’s more to it than just discipline?”
Mara hesitated, then signed, “A ward silently enjoys what her guardian offers.” Her movements were controlled, almost too controlled, as if she were holding something back.
Sonia and Anna exchanged glances, a flicker of amusement passing between them. Their fingers moved quickly, sharing a private joke, their eyes glinting with slightly lewd humor.
Mara watched them for a moment, then signed with a calm resolve, “Whatever you’ve heard about it, it’s probably true. It’s sometimes harsh, but I don’t wish to be without it anymore.” She paused, her hands slowing, the weight of her words sinking in. “That has not always been the case.”
Sonia and Anna looked at her, sensing there was more she hadn’t said. Mara met their gaze, her fingers moving with an almost ominous weight. “The device also has an edging mode. If discipline mode doesn’t bring a ward in line, that will do the trick.”
As the sun set, casting a golden light over the veranda, Philippe approached, signaling it was time to go.
Sonia and Anna began exchanging their veils for masks. Philippe unlocked Mara and helped her to her feet, guiding her. Henry and Julien released Sonia and Anna, preparing to leave.
Philippe, holding Mara by his side, nodded to Henry and Julien. “Thank you for coming. It was a pleasure.”
Henry smiled. “Likewise, Philippe. We look forward to the next time.”
With final curtsies, the group parted ways. Philippe led Mara inside, while Henry, Sonia, Julien, and Anna walked toward the tram stop.
As they waited, Sonia turned to Anna, her hands moving subtly. “The iGuardian in edging mode must be tough. I wonder what Mara did to deserve it.”
Anna nodded, signing back, “I can’t imagine the strain. I’d lose my mind.”
Their conversation was cut short by Henry, who caught Sonia’s small signs nonetheless and reprimanded her. “Sonia, no gossiping. I won’t tolerate it. Whatever Mara did, she’s been corrected, and that’s the end of it. You know better.”
Sonia quickly signed, “Yes, Sir. I apologize.” She knew exactly what kind of correction Henry might have in mind if she gossiped about edging, and she definitely didn’t want that experience. She hated being denied.
The tram arrived, and they boarded, finding locking seats for the women at the back. After clicking Sonia into place, Henry rested his hand on her shoulder, a reminder of his authority. Julien guided Anna to a seat opposite Sonia and locked her in.
As the tram began its journey, Sonia and Anna exchanged a few more silent gestures. Despite the restrictions, they found comfort in each other’s company. The ride home was quiet, filled with unspoken thoughts and the hope of future gatherings. For now, they found solace in knowing they weren’t alone.

title: Chapter 46: Two years ago: Decommissioning an Airport
content:
Two years ago: Decommissioning an Airport# Philippe stood by the large window of the villa, overlooking the garden where Mara was instructing the gardener. He watched her hands dance in the air, giving instructions, yet sticking to form in a way that came naturally to her now. The iGuardian had finally put to correct use, shaping her to the expectations of her role, but Philippe couldn’t help but reflect on how wrong he had been at the start.
He had thought pain would be enough to break her defiance, to mold her into the woman society expected her to be. But Mara wasn’t like the others. Pain had only made her more determined, more resistant. It was only when he discovered how to harness her desire, for release, but also for reward and for approval, that she began to change. Seeing her now, fully absorbed in her tasks, he realized how flawed his initial approach had been. He had underestimated her, not just in her resistance but in her potential.
As Mara continued her work, efficiently managing the household staff, Philippe allowed himself a moment of self-critique. He had kept her close, confined to the villa, thinking it was the best way to ensure she adjusted. He now recognized that decision for what it was—his own insecurity. He had been afraid to let her out, to risk her slipping back into her old ways. But Mara wasn’t meant to be contained; she needed something challenging, something that would engage her mind and give her a sense of purpose.
Philippe’s thoughts drifted to the city’s projects, the initiatives he had heard discussed in his network. Most weren’t suited to Mara, but then one idea came to him—the decommissioning of Geneva International Airport. The plan was to shrink it down to a heliport and find a new use for the vast space left behind. The soil was poisoned from years of pollution, and the task of rehabilitating it was daunting. But it was the kind of challenge that Mara could sink her teeth into, something that would demand the full extent of her abilities while keeping her within the bounds of what was socially acceptable for a Changed woman.
Philippe approached Mara as she finished her instructions to the gardener. He waited until she turned to him and began.
“Mara, I’ve been thinking about a project that might interest you,” Philippe began. “The decommissioning of Geneva International Airport. They’re reducing it to a heliport, but the land is heavily polluted. It needs a new purpose.”
Mara listened attentively. After thinking for a moment, she signed carefully, “That sounds like a significant challenge, Sir. If it pleases you, perhaps we could consider turning the area into a series of connected parks and community gardens? We might use modern biotechnology to help extract the pollutants from the soil. Over time, we could transform the concrete wasteland into green spaces—edible garden patches, small parks, areas that would serve the community.”
Philippe watched her, nodding slightly. “And how would you propose to manage this?”
Mara signed again, in precise and respectful movements. “Sir, if it suits your plans, the project could also serve as a place of learning and rehabilitation for women like myself, who might be struggling to adjust. These women could work in the garden, finding a sense of purpose within a structured environment. It would give them clear goals and expectations, something to focus on. Of course, it would require careful planning and oversight.”
She paused, then added, “I could draft a proposal. If it finds your approval, Sir, you could present it to the city council. I believe we could secure funding through national sustainability programs. If you think it’s appropriate, this project could align with both environmental and social needs.”
Philippe considered her words, then smiled approvingly. “That sounds promising, Mara. If we move forward, I’ll need you to draft those proposals. I will check them over and use my contacts to present them. You’ll need to navigate the city’s bureaucracy, find the right funding sources, and ensure the project aligns with societal expectations. Maybe I will use you to convince a few key people. Are you prepared to handle that?”
Mara nodded, her hands moving in a graceful sign of agreement. “Yes, Sir. I would be honored to take on the task. I believe this project could truly benefit the community.”
Philippe placed a hand on her shoulder. “Good girl. Start on the proposals. This is your project, but I’ll support you where needed. Make it count.”
Mara signed her thanks and curtsied. “Thank you, Sir. I’ll begin immediately.”
With that, Philippe turned and left her to her thoughts, confident that Mara’s brilliant mind would bring this project to life, and in doing so, help her and others find their place in this new world.
A few days later, as Philippe entered his study, he was surprised to find Mara kneeling next to his desk. She was secured to a fempad, her body locked in place by the post behind her. The locking mechanism attached not only to her corset but also to her neck corset, with her elbows and wrists pressed tightly into self-locking manacles. She couldn’t move, couldn’t do anything without his intervention. He had no way of knowing how long she’d been there.
Ignoring her for a moment, Philippe turned his attention to the stack of folders on his desk. Each was meticulously prepared: proposals for councilmen, social media campaigns, suggestions for the school and reformatory boards, grant applications for the national sustainability board. And then there was a purple folder—documents inside that should not exist and that he knew could be used to sway even the most stubborn council members or board officials. Philippe knew Mara was talented, even ruthless, but seeing this level of preparation for the community garden project was astonishing.
He took his time reviewing everything, letting her stay in her self-imposed confinement. She had gone to extraordinary lengths, even in how she restrained herself, ensuring complete immobilization without anyone’s help.
Finally, after carefully reading through all the documents, he leaned back in his chair, thoroughly impressed. He turned to Mara and began unlocking her wrists and arms, allowing her to move and sign again. Then he squatted down in front of her, looking her in the eye.
“Now, what is all this?” he asked.
Mara’s hands moved gracefully as she signed, her tone polite and hopeful. “Sir, I’ve prepared everything needed for the community garden project. These folders contain proposals, strategies, and plans. If you approve, you can use all of this to move the project forward. I wanted to ensure everything was ready for your review.”
Philippe nodded, watching her closely. “And locking yourself like this?”
Mara’s hands hesitated for just a moment before continuing. “Sir, I wanted to make sure I couldn’t take any action without your permission, ensuring I would stick to form. This was the only way I could think of to absolutely ensure that.”
Philippe considered her response, his gaze softening slightly. She had gone above and beyond, not just in her work but in her commitment to following his guidance.
“You’ve done an exceptional job, Mara,” he said, his voice steady. “This is impressive. You’ve thought of everything.”
Mara signed her thanks, her movements full of quiet hope. “Thank you, Sir. I just want to help make this project a success.”
Philippe smiled, finally releasing her other restraints. “You’ve certainly done your part. Let’s move forward with this. You’ve earned it.”
Mara got up, then curtsied, her hands signing. “Thank you, Sir. I’m ready to follow your lead.”
The following weeks were a whirlwind of activity for Philippe. He sent out proposals, scheduled appointments, and made official presentations while also meeting key figures informally over dinner. Mara, meanwhile, executed the social media grassroots campaigns she had meticulously planned, carefully timing each release for maximum impact. Together, their efforts created a perfect storm of political pressure on the city council, which coincided with the arrival of several grants—most of them approved—offering a straightforward solution. The council, finding themselves cornered by public demand and the sudden availability of funding, had little choice but to greenlight the community garden project.
At a dinner at Councillor Laurent’s home, Philippe and the Councillor were seated outside on the veranda, each with a glass of wine in hand. The evening air was crisp, and the low hum of conversation drifted from inside the house. After some light small talk, the Councillor swirled his wine and shifted the conversation to business.
“So, Philippe,” Laurent began, “with the community garden project about to be approved by the city council tomorrow, we’ll need someone to lead it. Do you have anyone in mind?”
Philippe paused for a moment, glancing back inside the house. Through the large glass doors, he saw Mara and Councillor Laurent’s wife, Claire, signing animatedly to each other. Claire was dressed in a daring gown that pushed the boundaries of Changed society’s modesty standards. The vivid, blocking color patterns of her dress caught the eye, and the fabric barely covered enough to be considered compliant. Her half-mask was more of a decorative piece than an actual covering, and the tiny hat perched on her head seemed to mock the idea of modesty altogether.
Mara, in contrast, was dressed in a way that emphasized her submission and discipline. Her burgundy gown was rich and elegant, the deep color highlighting the strictness of her attire. The gown’s bodice was tightly corseted, cinching her waist severely and pushing her posture into perfect alignment. Matching gloves covered her arms up to her elbows, and a bonnet, tightly tied under her chin, framed her masked face. The mask itself was full, hiding every feature except for her expressive eyes, which flicked up occasionally to meet Philippe’s gaze before returning to Claire.
Philippe turned back to Laurent. “Mara would be my recommendation. Before the Change, she was a corporate contract lawyer, highly skilled. If you consider it appropriate to have a woman lead the project, she would be more than capable.”
Laurent took a sip of his wine, considering Philippe’s words. “That would be legally impossible under the new laws,” he said, his tone thoughtful. “But… there is a workaround. Philippe Beaumont, represented through his ward Mara, could be a viable solution. Under the reformed guardianship laws, you would bear full liability for her actions, but she could effectively lead the project.”
Philippe hesitated, weighing the implications. The responsibility would be immense, not only for the project but also for the legal and financial consequences of any missteps. Yet he knew Mara’s capabilities, her drive, and her attention to detail. She had already done the lion’s share of the work to bring the project to this point.
After a moment, Philippe nodded. “I agree,” he said firmly. “Mara will represent me in leading the project. I’ll take full responsibility.”
Laurent smiled, satisfied with the decision. “Then it’s settled. I’ll make the arrangements, and we’ll announce it after the council meeting tomorrow.”
As the men raised their glasses in a silent toast, Philippe glanced back at Mara once more. The flickering candlelight caught the gleam of her mask, and for a brief moment, he saw the determination in her eyes. He knew she was ready for this challenge, and he was prepared to stand behind her, no matter the cost.
The following day, the Community Garden Project was formally established at the City Council meeting and Philippe Beaumont, represented by his ward Mara, was appointed to lead it.

title: Chapter 47: Plans involving Art and Fashion
Chapter 48: A Night at the Opera
content:
A Night at the Opera# Philippe had arranged for a limousine with a driver for the evening. He helped Mara down the stairs, and the driver adjusted the fempad in the back to accommodate her voluminous dress. Despite the cumbersome outfit, Mara knelt and locked into the seat’s holding arms with ease, the security cushions positioned carefully to avoid ruining her attire. Philippe sat opposite her, and they headed to the Grand Théâtre. The twenty-minute drive from Cologny passed quickly.
Upon arrival, Philippe unlocked Mara and helped her out of the car and into the grand theater. The foyer was grand, with chandeliers casting a warm glow over marble floors and intricate woodwork. A sweeping staircase with rich red carpeting invited guests to the upper levels.
The atmosphere at the opera was one of refined elegance, wrapped in formality and ritual. Women in elaborate, restrictive dresses moved gracefully through the foyer, their faces hidden behind veils or ornate masks. The majority of them wore face masks and had their hands free so they could hand-dance, while those in veils were often manacled, their hands bound behind or in front of them. They would have to use voice to articulate their needs. The soft murmur of male voices was the only real sound, aside from the occasional clink of jewelry, chains, or the rustle of fabric.
By the bar, men stood beside high-top marble tables with cast-iron feet. The tables had steel rings in the center, where many guardians had leashed their wards. It was a common sight—women standing still, tethered by their wrists or collars, waiting patiently while their guardians mingled or visited the washroom. A line of tether bars stretched along one wall, with women held in place, their feet locked into heel restraints and hands secured behind them to manacle bars, while their guardians were occupied.
Mara watched quietly as a small commotion caught her attention. A young woman, her face hidden behind a delicate veil, used her voice—shrill and loud. This was unusual—most women tried to avoid using voice entirely, and when they needed to speak, they certainly wouldn’t be loud or use any of the words or phrases that Mara had overheard. Her guardian, calm but firm, motioned for her to stop, but she didn’t. He finally led her to a quiet corner, where she stood facing the wall, clearly expected to calm down before she could address him appropriately.
As her gaze drifted further through the foyer, she saw a family approach. A father led his wife and two daughters in a typical chain-train. He held a leash attached to his wife’s collar, and she, in turn, held the leash of their eldest daughter, who led her younger sister by another leash. All three women were dressed fashionably: sparkling dresses and highly decorated masks, their tight dresses making it seem as if they glided effortlessly toward their booth.
Philippe scanned the crowd and soon spotted Henry with Sonia. Henry’s classic style never seemed to go out of fashion. He wore a formal evening jacket with satin lapels and a red fez, adding a touch of whimsy. The bright color was striking against the monochrome palette of his outfit.
Sonia’s harem dress was crafted from delicate white chiffon veils. Each layer was sheer by itself, but together they provided just enough coverage, with a teasing hint of what lay beneath. The bodice featured a sweetheart neckline adorned with silver embroidery. Instead of leaving the midriff bare like a traditional harem-girl outfit, a sleek, silvery corset cinched her waist, offering both modesty and a sculpted silhouette. The corset was seamlessly integrated into the design, its polished surface reflecting the light and creating a striking contrast with the soft chiffon veils cascading over her figure.
The skirt, made of additional chiffon veils, flowed gracefully, hinting at the shape of her legs without fully revealing them. High heels and ankle manacles restricted her steps to small, elegant movements. Long, flowing sleeves ended in steel cuffs that connected her wrists to her waist at the back. A heavy steel collar encircled her neck, attached to a chain held by Henry. Her head was crowned with a white and silver fez that matched Henry’s, serving as the anchor for the many layers of veils. Though the veils were thin, together they almost—but not quite—obscured her face.
